Many people ignore strange sensations in their legs until the pain becomes severe. But your body often gives warning signs much earlier.
If you experience tingling in legs, burning sensation in legs, or a constant pins and needles sensation, it could be a sign of nerve pain in leg caused by irritation or compression of nerves.
One of the most common reasons behind these symptoms is sciatica nerve pain, where the sciatic nerve gets irritated in the lower back or hip. This can lead to leg numbness causes, tingling in legs, and sometimes even leg weakness causes. Many people also experience a burning sensation in legs that travels down the thigh or calf.
In some cases, nerve compression symptoms can develop due to prolonged sitting, poor posture, disc irritation, or tight muscles. When the nerve is irritated, it can produce sensations like pins and needles sensation, tingling in legs, or sharp nerve pain in leg.
Another possible reason for these symptoms is peripheral neuropathy symptoms, where nerves become sensitive and start sending abnormal signals like burning sensation in legs, numbness, or weakness.
Sometimes people also notice leg swelling causes along with heaviness and discomfort, which may increase pressure around nerves and worsen sciatica symptoms or nerve compression symptoms.
The good news is that many of these problems can improve with proper physiotherapy for nerve pain.

At first glance, it looks like this person is simply strapped to a moving table... but what if I told you this machine is actually creating space inside the spine to help relieve back pain and sciatica?
What you're seeing is Spinal Decompression Therapy, a specialized non-surgical treatment commonly used for people suffering from chronic lower back pain, sciatica, bulging discs, herniated discs, and certain degenerative spinal conditions.
So how does it work?
The motorized table applies a gentle, controlled pulling force to the lumbar spine (lower back). This creates a process called **decompression**, where the vertebrae are slightly separated, reducing pressure on the spinal discs and nearby nerves.
Why is this important?
🦴 Reduces Disc Pressure
Spinal discs act as shock absorbers between your vertebrae. When a disc bulges or herniates, it can press on nearby nerves and cause pain, numbness, or tingling down the leg. Decompression may help reduce this pressure.
💧 Improves Nutrient Exchange
Unlike many tissues in the body, spinal discs have a very limited blood supply. The gentle stretching and relaxation cycles help encourage the movement of water, oxygen, and nutrients into the discs, supporting their health and recovery.
While spinal decompression can be beneficial for the right patient, it isn't a one-size-fits-all solution. A proper assessment is always important to determine the root cause of your pain.

Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis) is more than just shoulder pain or muscle tightness.
Many people believe it develops from overuse, but the real problem often occurs inside the shoulder joint capsule.
As inflammation builds, the capsule gradually thickens and stiffens, leading to shoulder stiffness, limited shoulder mobility, and difficulty performing simple daily activities like reaching overhead, dressing, or sleeping comfortably.
What makes frozen shoulder unique is its strong association with diabetes, thyroid disorders, and hormonal changes. These underlying conditions can influence the tissues surrounding the joint and increase the risk of developing adhesive capsulitis.
The good news? Early clinical assessment and the right physiotherapy approach can help manage pain, improve shoulder mobility, restore movement, and support shoulder rehabilitation.
Treatment is most effective when tailored to the stage of the condition rather than using the same exercises for everyone.
If your shoulder movement is gradually decreasing, don't ignore the warning signs. Understanding the cause is the first step toward recovery.

A controlled traction technique helps decompress the joint surfaces, allowing them to move more freely with less restriction.
Why does this matter?
When joints become stiff, your body starts compensating during walking, squatting, climbing stairs, and even simple daily activities. Over time, these movement compensations can contribute to discomfort, reduced mobility, and unnecessary strain on surrounding muscles.

I visited this therapy center for treatment of my cervical spine, shoulder condition, and nerve-related symptoms. While I understand that inflammation management requires time, I was concerned that my treatment mainly consisted of repeated laser sessions without a proper physical reassessment.

Though i was patiently waiting but for the past 3-4 days, I was consistently requesting a detailed physical examination and reassessment by the consulting doctor to better understand my condition and treatment plan. Unfortunately, this did not happen despite multiple attempts.

On one occasion, I visited with a family member. We were made to wait for nearly two hours & When I finally got the opportunity to speak with the consulting doctor and requested a physical examination, she responded by saying, “I will finish my work and you will have to wait for another twenty minutes. If you want a reassessment, then I will do it.”

After already waiting for a long time, this response felt dismissive. When I politely mentioned that a physical assessment would take only a few minutes, there was no clarification provided and she left the room. After waiting another 20–25 minutes, we were called in again, but there was still reluctance in conducting a proper physical examination. I was told that my condition had already been checked and the treatment would continue as planned.

I have paid a substantial amount for my treatment, and as a patient, I understand that I have the right to seek clarification, request reassessment, and ask questions regarding my care at any stage. Expecting transparency, respectful communication, and periodic evaluation is not unreasonable — it is a basic standard of professional healthcare.

Unfortunately, I did not experience the level of professionalism and transparency I expected and the behaviour was quite rude .

I hope the center improves its patient communication, timely assessments, and overall approach so that patients feel heard, respected, and properly evaluated.

featured_reviews.name: C I
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had the pleasure of working with Dr. Yukta after a challenging period of physical recovery. A few months ago, I suffered a backward fall, resulting in sutures on my head. Just weeks before, I had undergone surgery to remove a large abscess from my stomach, which also required 15 sutures. During this time, I experienced significant pain and difficulty walking, particularly in my legs.

Dr. Yukta provided several physiotherapy sessions that have been incredibly effective in my recovery. Thanks to her guidance, I am now able to move without discomfort. What sets Dr. Yukta apart is not only her professionalism and expertise but also the personal attention she gives during each session. She takes the time to explain the purpose behind every exercise, which has helped me understand the importance of each step in my healing process.

Her treatment goes beyond just physical therapy; it has been emotionally therapeutic as well. I’ve made remarkable progress under her care, and I am deeply grateful for her support in my recovery journey.

featured_reviews.name: Sejal Mhatre
featured_reviews.review_text:
My mother was diagnosed with Spine TB, which resulted in an infection in her lower spinal cord. This infection caused damage to the nerves connected to her legs, leading to significant mobility issues. Initially, she was unable to walk properly and required a walker for assistance. Unfortunately, her condition worsened, and she lost all leg power, necessitating immediate surgery. After undergoing a successful surgery, she was recommended physiotherapy to regain strength in her legs.

Dr. Yukta was assigned to provide home-based physiotherapy sessions. Over the course of two months, Dr. Yukta diligently conducted leg exercises, gradually improving my mother's condition. Within the first month, she was able to move her feet on the bed and subsequently, with the support of a walker, she began to stand independently. Through consistent and dedicated physiotherapy sessions my mother's progress accelerated and she was able to walk slowly with the walker in just 15 days.

Dr. Yukta's positive and encouraging approach played a crucial role in this remarkable recovery. Today, two months after the initial therapy, my mother is able to walk independently without the aid of a walker. We are confident that she will fully recover and return to her normal routine within the next month.

We extend our sincere gratitude to Dr. Yukta for her exceptional care, expertise, and positive influence. Her dedication and effective sessions have significantly contributed to my mother's recovery and improved quality of life. 😊
